insights.methodology: Derived from bank_financials/SBACBANK/quarterly/*.json (FY2013-FY2025 year-end, Solo basis) and ratios_timeseries.json. SBAC Bank was licensed in 2013, so this series is the bank's complete public history (no FY2011/FY2012). Every figure is either a reported value from the bank's own audited Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Basel Pillar III capital disclosure, or 'Highlights on the overall activities of the bank' annexure, or an explicitly labelled calculation from two or more such reported figures (documented per-item in the quarterly files); FY2025's provision-shortfall and required-capital figures are quoted directly from the Independent Auditor's qualified opinion / Emphasis of Matter. FY2017 is recovered from the FY2018 report's own audited comparative column because FY2017's own report's financial-statement pages did not extract (a pdftotext failure, not a scan). No figure is interpolated, estimated without disclosure of the method, or backfilled from a different period. Every number cited below was verified programmatically against quarterly/*.json before this file was written.

risk_signals.statement: The Independent Auditor issued a QUALIFIED OPINION for FY2025 -- the only qualified opinion in this bank's 13-year archive -- citing a provision shortfall of Tk.1,023.57 crore (10,235.7m): required provision was Tk.1,379.40 crore (13,794.0m) against provision actually maintained of only Tk.355.83 crore (3,558.3m, all categories). The shortfall alone equals 91.6% of the Bank's entire total shareholders' equity of Tk.11,174.66m. The auditors state explicitly that had the shortfall been fully recognised, the Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) -- reported at 13.40%, only 0.90 percentage points above the 12.50% regulatory minimum -- would have fallen below that minimum. A specific, named example within the shortfall: Tk.158.66 crore of fixed deposits placed with non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs) matured long ago and are considered doubtful of recovery, against which the Bank held ZERO provision as at 31 December 2025.

Classified (non-performing) loans grew from Tk.5,149.57m (FY2023, NPL ratio 5.93%) to Tk.14,332.62m (FY2024, NPL ratio 16.17%) to Tk.18,814.94m (FY2025, NPL ratio 19.87%) -- a 265% increase in classified loans and a more-than-tripling of the NPL ratio in two years. This is the same sector-wide asset-quality recognition event documented across the DSE banking dataset for FY2024, but at SBAC it continued to worsen materially through FY2025 rather than stabilising. Provision coverage against classified loans (provision held specifically against classified loans, on a basis consistent across FY2019-FY2025) fell from 30.22% in FY2024 to 12.60% in FY2025 -- the Bank REDUCED classified-loan provisioning in absolute terms (from Tk.4,331.35m to Tk.2,371.25m) even as the classified-loan balance grew a further 31.3%.

Profit after tax fell 79.7% from Tk.536.61m (FY2023) to Tk.108.73m (FY2024), then a further 94.0% to Tk.6.50m (FY2025) -- essentially break-even. Return on Equity fell from 4.89% (FY2023) to 0.98% (FY2024) to 0.06% (FY2025); Return on Assets fell from 0.48% to 0.09% to 0.01% over the same span, even as total assets kept growing (Tk.117,521.67m to Tk.132,911.98m across the two years). Capital adequacy ratios barely moved over the same period (CRAR 13.71% to 13.80% to 13.40%), meaning the reported capital position did not visibly signal the scale of the profitability and provisioning deterioration -- see the provision-shortfall signal above for why.

Net interest income (interest income minus interest expense) fell 53.1% in a single year, from Tk.1,909.23m (FY2024) to Tk.895.22m (FY2025), because interest income was essentially flat (Tk.8,577.22m to Tk.8,565.55m, -0.1%) while interest expense grew 15.0% (Tk.6,667.98m to Tk.7,670.34m) -- i.e. the cost of funding rose sharply while lending yields did not keep pace. Using net interest income over period-end gross loans as a proxy for margin, this fell from 4.48% in FY2019 to a range of 1.6%-2.5% in FY2020-FY2024 and then to 0.95% in FY2025, its lowest point in the series. Combined with the provision and asset-quality signals above, SBAC Bank's core lending business generated very little of its (already minimal) FY2025 earnings; investment income (Tk.2,150.15m) was more than twice net interest income.

Following a Bangladesh Bank directive (letter BSD-5/106/2026-403), SBAC Bank PLC paid no dividend at all for FY2025 -- the Bank's own disclosure states it lacked sufficient profit (Tk.0.65 crore) to cover the combined provision and tax shortfall (Tk.1,023.57 crore) while remaining above minimum capital requirements. Bangladesh Bank's letter explicitly linked the non-dividend decision to the risk that fully recognising the specific-provision shortfall would drop the Bank's capital below the regulatory minimum. The consecutive non-dividend years that resulted triggered a technical 'Z-Category' reclassification of the stock on the exchange, a market-facing consequence beyond the financial statements themselves.

The FY2025 crisis was foreshadowed in the Bank's own FY2024 annual report: its own 'Highlights on the overall activities of the bank' annexure for FY2024 already disclosed a provision deficit ('Surplus/(deficit) provision against loans and advances') of Tk.6,558,390,257 (6,558.39m) against loans and advances, equal to 59.4% of that year's total shareholders' equity (Tk.11,045.53m) -- a full year before the auditor's FY2025 qualified opinion made the much larger (Tk.10,235.7m) shortfall explicit. This indicates the underlying asset-quality and provisioning problem was building for at least two reporting cycles before it produced a qualified audit opinion.

SBAC Bank started life extremely well-capitalised, as is typical for a newly-licensed bank: CRAR was 61.98% in its first year (FY2013), falling steadily as the balance sheet grew into its capital base -- 29.54% (FY2014), 21.19% (FY2015), 18.59% (FY2016), 16.54% (FY2017), 15.88% (FY2018) -- before settling in a 13.4%-14.7% band from FY2019 onward, still above the 12.50% (Basel III, with conservation buffer) regulatory minimum in every year of the series including the stressed FY2025 (13.40%). This is a normal maturation path, not itself a warning sign, but by FY2025 the cushion above the regulatory minimum (0.90 percentage points) had become thin enough that the auditor's disclosed provision shortfall was explicitly flagged as capable of breaching it if recognised in full.

Total assets grew from Tk.8,673.89m (FY2013) to Tk.132,911.98m (FY2025), a 15.3-fold increase (approximately 25.5% compound annual growth over 12 years), while gross loans grew 31.4-fold (Tk.3,006.77m to Tk.94,458.10m) over the same span. Asset quality was excellent for most of that growth: classified loans were nil in FY2013, FY2014 and FY2016 (FY2015 not disclosed in extractable text), and the NPL ratio stayed below 2% through FY2018 (0.87% FY2017, 1.97% FY2018) before rising gradually to a 5.2%-6.2% range in FY2019-FY2023 (6.09%, 6.22%, 5.85%, 5.17%, 5.93% respectively) and then sharply in FY2024-FY2025 (see the asset-quality signal above). The rapid loan growth outpacing deposit growth in some years (e.g. FY2022 loan growth 18.25% vs deposit growth 15.73%, or FY2017 loan growth 43.45% vs deposit growth 30.74%) is consistent with, though does not on its own prove, the credit-quality strains that emerged from FY2024.

Newly-sourced Q1-Q3 2024 unaudited quarterly filings show the FY2024 asset-quality crisis (already known from the FY2024 annual report: NPL 5.93%->16.17%, provision shortfall exploding to Tk.6,558.39m) was concentrated ENTIRELY in Q4 2024. The Solo NPL ratio was essentially flat and low through the first three quarters -- 5.90% (Q1), 6.16% (Q2), 6.52% (Q3), against a 5.93% base at 31-Dec-2023 -- and the loans-and-advances-only provision shortfall (Note 8.10) actually SHRANK for three consecutive quarters: Tk.266.73m (Q1) to Tk.182.68m (Q2) to just Tk.77.39m (Q3), down from Tk.355.64m at 31-Dec-2023. Nine-month cumulative PAT was a healthy Tk.770.60m (up sharply from FY2023's equivalent Tk.459.74m), yet full-year FY2024 PAT was only Tk.108.73m -- implying Q4 2024 ALONE swung to a net LOSS of approximately Tk.661.87m and added Tk.8,721.29m in newly classified loans (NPL jumping 6.52%->16.17%, +9.65 percentage points), the single largest one-quarter deterioration found anywhere in this bank's dataset. This is the clearest evidence available that the FY2024 recognition event was a year-end/audit-driven shock rather than a gradually-building problem.

In sharp contrast to FY2024's single-quarter shock, newly-sourced Q1-Q3 2025 filings show the FY2025 deterioration built up progressively. The Solo NPL ratio rose every quarter -- 16.17% (31-Dec-2024) to 16.37% (Q1, +0.20pp) to 16.98% (Q2, +0.61pp) to 19.80% (Q3, +2.82pp, by far the single largest quarterly move) to ~19.87% (Q4/year-end, Consolidated-basis proxy, +0.07pp) -- and the loans-and-advances-only provision shortfall grew from Tk.6,558.39m (Dec-2024) to Tk.6,556.94m (Q1, flat) to Tk.7,361.52m (Q2, +Tk.804.6m) to Tk.8,019.93m (Q3, +Tk.658.4m). Unlike the NPL/shortfall trend, the PROFIT impact was still deferred to Q4: discrete quarterly PAT was Tk.109.51m (Q1), Tk.4.31m (Q2) and Tk.3.88m (Q3) -- already collapsing but still marginally positive -- before an implied Q4 net LOSS of approximately Tk.111.19m (full-year PAT of Tk.6.50m minus the 9-month cumulative Tk.117.69m) driven by a Q4 provision charge (~Tk.340.2m implied) nearly two-thirds the size of the entire first nine months' combined charge (Tk.526.71m). Q1-2025 profit was already down 43.6% year-on-year versus Q1-2024 (Tk.109.51m vs Tk.194.09m) -- i.e. unlike FY2024, the FY2025 decline was visible from the very first quarter of the year, not just at year-end.

Comparing each newly-sourced FY2024/FY2025 interim quarter against its own same-quarter prior-year figure (all now in this dataset) shows a complete reversal in trend. FY2024's cumulative PAT was UP year-on-year in every interim quarter -- Q1 +47.3% (Tk.194.09m vs Tk.131.77m), Q2 +17.8% (Tk.378.78m vs Tk.321.49m cumulative), Q3 +67.6% (Tk.770.60m vs Tk.459.74m cumulative) -- meaning FY2024 was tracking as a materially BETTER year than FY2023 right up until its Q4 collapse. FY2025's equivalent comparisons were negative from the first quarter and worsened every quarter: Q1 -43.6%, Q2 -70.0% (cumulative), Q3 -84.7% (cumulative). The two years' interim trajectories are near-mirror-opposites of each other despite both ending in a similarly weak full-year result (Tk.108.73m and Tk.6.50m respectively) -- FY2024's weakness was invisible until year-end, FY2025's was visible from Q1 onward.

Every quarterly filing sourced this pass cites a Bangladesh Bank Department of Off-site Supervision letter (ref. DOS(CAMS)1157/41(dividend)/YYYY-NNNN) approving deferral of that period's loans-and-advances provision shortfall until the next annual financial statements are finalized: letter ...2023-2113 (25 Apr 2023, a ~Tk.370m gap), ...2024-1836 (30 Apr 2024, a ~Tk.355.6m gap carried from FY2023), and ...2025-3115 (22 May 2025, by which point the gap -- now measured on an all-categories basis including NBFI placements -- had grown to Tk.11,430.1m and required a formal qualified audit opinion). The reconstructed loans-and-advances-only shortfall series across all quarters now in this dataset is: -Tk.370.0m (Dec-2022) -> -Tk.370.0m (Mar-2023) -> -Tk.369.9m (Jun-2023) -> -Tk.277.4m (Sep-2023) -> -Tk.355.64m (Dec-2023) -> -Tk.266.73m (Mar-2024) -> -Tk.182.68m (Jun-2024) -> -Tk.77.39m (Sep-2024) -> -Tk.6,558.39m (Dec-2024, an approximately 85-fold single-quarter jump) -> -Tk.6,556.94m (Mar-2025) -> -Tk.7,361.52m (Jun-2025) -> -Tk.8,019.93m (Sep-2025). The same annual forbearance mechanism that comfortably accommodated a stable, shrinking ~Tk.300-370m gap for two full years was still in use, unchanged, when the gap it was deferring grew by more than an order of magnitude within a single reporting year.

SBAC Bank's own Q2-2025 unaudited quarterly financial statement (Note 8.10, required-provision table footnote) states verbatim: 'Maximum allowable provision has been made in current quarter keeping EPS only Taka 0.005.' This is a direct, bank-authored disclosure that Q2-2025 provisioning (Tk.182.81m for that discrete quarter) was set at the highest level the Bank judged compatible with still reporting a positive (barely above zero) quarterly EPS, rather than a level determined solely by assessed credit risk on the loan book. Discrete Q2-2025 PAT was Tk.4.31m on EPS of exactly 0.005 -- consistent with the disclosure. This is one of the more direct pieces of evidence in this entire dataset of provisioning being managed toward an earnings outcome.

insights.historical_context: SBAC Bank (South Bangla Agriculture & Commerce Bank, renamed SBAC Bank PLC in 2023) was incorporated in February 2013 and licensed the following month, making this 13-year series (FY2013-FY2025) its entire public history -- there is no FY2011 or FY2012 for this bank, unlike most others in this dataset. Its first decade was a conventional growth story for a fourth-generation Bangladeshi bank: total assets compounded at roughly 25.5% a year to reach Tk.132.9 billion by FY2025, capital adequacy declined from an extraordinarily high starting point (61.98% CRAR in FY2013) to a comfortable-but-thinning mid-teens band as the balance sheet matured, and asset quality was essentially pristine through FY2018 (NPL ratio never above 2%). That picture changed decisively from FY2024. Classified loans nearly tripled the NPL ratio in two years (5.93% in FY2023 to 16.17% in FY2024 to 19.87% in FY2025), profit after tax collapsed by more than 98% cumulatively over the same span (Tk.536.61m to Tk.108.73m to Tk.6.50m) and, critically, provisioning did not keep pace: the Bank's own FY2024 annexure disclosed a Tk.6.56 billion provision deficit (59% of that year's equity), and the FY2025 Independent Auditor's Report escalated this to a formal qualified opinion, quantifying a Tk.10,235.7m shortfall (91.6% of FY2025 equity) between required provision (Tk.13,794.0m) and provision actually held (Tk.3,558.3m) -- including a specific, fully-unprovided Tk.1,586.6m of doubtful NBFI placements. Reported capital ratios remained nominally compliant throughout (CRAR never fell below the 12.50% regulatory minimum in this series, reading 13.40% in FY2025), but the auditors themselves state that recognising the full provision shortfall would breach that minimum -- the same recognition-versus-deferral pattern documented at other DSE banks in FY2024-FY2025, here compounding into FY2025 rather than resolving. Bangladesh Bank directed the Bank to pay no FY2025 dividend, and the resulting run of non-dividend years produced a technical 'Z-Category' reclassification on the exchange -- a market-visible consequence layered on top of the financial-statement findings. A subsequent pass sourced Q1-Q3 unaudited quarterly filings for FY2023-2025 (plus FY2016 Q2-Q3) directly from the Bank's own investors-relations document archive, revealing that FY2024 and FY2025 deteriorated in almost opposite ways intra-year. FY2024 gave no interim warning at all: NPL stayed in a narrow 5.90%-6.52% band and the provision shortfall actually shrank every quarter through Q3 (to just Tk.77.39m), with 9-month PAT (Tk.770.60m) running well ahead of FY2023's pace -- before Q4 2024 alone added Tk.8.72 billion in newly classified loans and swung to an implied ~Tk.661.9m net loss, the single sharpest one-quarter reversal in this dataset. FY2025, by contrast, gave clear warning from the start: Q1-2025 profit was already down 43.6% year-on-year, and both the NPL ratio (16.17% to 19.80% by Q3) and the provision shortfall (Tk.6,558m to Tk.8,020m by Q3) climbed every quarter, with the profit impact only fully landing in an implied ~Tk.111.2m Q4 net loss. Three consecutive Bangladesh Bank forbearance letters (2023, 2024, 2025, each deferring that year's shortfall into the next annual report) bridge the two years -- the same regulatory mechanism that comfortably covered a stable ~Tk.300-370m gap in FY2022-2023 was still the vehicle used once the gap it was deferring had grown roughly 18x on a loans-only basis (Tk.355.64m to Tk.6,558.39m) and over 30x on the later all-categories measure used in the FY2025 auditor's qualified opinion (Tk.355.64m to Tk.11,430.1m). SBAC Bank's own Q2-2025 filing explicitly states that quarter's provisioning was capped 'keeping EPS only Taka 0.005' -- a rare direct, bank-authored acknowledgement of earnings-targeted provisioning rather than pure risk-based provisioning.
insights.data_gaps: This series covers FY2013-FY2025, the bank's complete public history (it did not exist before 2013), for Q4/year-end (audited) periods. A subsequent pass added Q1-Q3 unaudited interim quarters for FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 (9 quarter-files, all validated: balance-sheet identity, equity-component sums, and income-statement sub-totals all reconcile exactly or to within Tk.1-2 rounding in every file), plus FY2016 Q2-Q3 as a low-cost bonus (the earliest interim filings the Bank's own site lists; 2013-2015 and 2016-Q1 are CONFIRMED UNAVAILABLE -- no interim filings exist for those periods at all, not merely unresearched). Q1-Q3 interim data for FY2017-FY2022 and FY2026 Q1-Q2 remains a genuine, addressable gap: these quarters exist as listed, downloadable filings on the Bank's own site (same URL pattern as the periods already sourced) but were not reached in this pass, which prioritized FY2023-2025 per explicit instruction. FY2024's Q1-Q3 discrete-quarter columns do not exactly reconcile against cumulative-minus-prior-cumulative (small ~3-7% gaps, see 2024_Q2.json/2024_Q3.json) despite each filing being internally consistent alone -- an unexplained minor cross-report inconsistency specific to FY2024 (FY2023's and FY2025's equivalent quarters reconcile exactly). No capital-adequacy (CRAR/RWA/Tier1/Tier2) disclosure exists in any Q1-Q3 interim filing sourced this pass -- Basel III Pillar III disclosures are annual-report-only throughout this bank's archive, unlike the balance sheet/P&L/asset-quality notes which are common to both. FY2017 is not taken from its own annual report because that report's financial-statement pages (Balance Sheet, P&L, Cash Flow, Capital Structure/Adequacy) extract with headings but no numeric rows -- a pdftotext failure rather than a scan; every FY2017 figure here instead comes from the FY2018 report's own audited comparative column or from narrative/5-year-table citations in other reports, and its Tier-I/Tier-II capital split was not recoverable at all. Classified loans and NPL ratio for FY2014 and FY2015 were not found in any extractable text and are recorded as explicit gaps (bracketed by confirmed nil values in FY2013 and FY2016, but not themselves confirmed). Tier-I/Tier-II absolute capital amounts (Tk.) are gaps for FY2019-FY2025 (only Total Capital, CRAR and RWA -- all mutually reconciling -- were found on a clearly Solo-specific basis in extractable text for those years); the Tier-I/Tier-II ratio split (%) is additionally available (Solo-specific) for FY2019-FY2020 but not FY2021-FY2025, where the only CET1/Tier2 ratio narratives found were Consolidated-basis and were not applied to Solo totals to avoid mixing bases. FY2018's Tier-I/Tier-II absolute amounts are 'calculated' (reported ratio x reported RWA) rather than directly read, because that year's Pillar III sub-table was OCR-corrupted. FY2025's classified-loans and NPL-ratio figures are Consolidated-basis (the only basis found in extractable text), used as a close Solo proxy since the Bank's only subsidiary does not lend. EPS and, in some years, NAV per share are affected throughout the series by a recurring (and internally well-understood, arithmetically verified) BAS 33 bonus-share retrospective-restatement pattern -- see sources.json for the full explanation; every year's own first-published figure is used, with every later divergence documented rather than silently reconciled. No dividend, market-price, or share-count/branch/employee count data was systematically extracted for this pass (only where it appeared incidentally alongside a needed figure).

sources.reporting_basis: SOLO / STANDALONE throughout FY2013-FY2025. For FY2013-FY2020 the bank had no subsidiary, so its single 'Balance Sheet' / 'Profit and Loss Account' / 'Highlights on the overall activities of the bank' annexure are unambiguously Solo (=Consolidated by construction). SBAC Bank Investment Limited (a small, non-lending investment/brokerage subsidiary) first appears in the FY2021 annual report, from which point each report publishes both a 'Consolidated Balance Sheet'/'Consolidated Financial Highlights on the overall activities of the bank' AND a separate plain 'Balance Sheet'/'Highlights on the overall activities of the bank' (Solo). This dataset uses the Solo figures throughout FY2021-FY2025, per the project's standing preference for Solo over Consolidated. Confirmed by matching total assets, total deposits and total loans recorded in the Solo 'Highlights' annexure against the same year's own unlabelled ('Solo') Balance Sheet -- they are identical (e.g. FY2021 Solo Balance Sheet total assets 98,172,322,252 = Solo Highlights annexure total assets 98,172,322,252), whereas the Consolidated Balance Sheet for the same year (line ~14240 of the FY2021 report) shows a different total assets figure (97,813,747,714 Consolidated Financial Highlights). Solo vs Consolidated total assets differ by under 0.4% in every year FY2021-2025 (the subsidiary is small and does not lend -- 'Total loans and advances' is identical Solo vs Consolidated in FY2021), so the choice of basis is confirmed but not decision-critical to any conclusion in this dataset. FY2025's classified-loans/NPL-ratio figures are the one exception: they were only found in extractable text on a Consolidated basis (from the Directors' Report's own 5-year table and the auditor's narrative); given the subsidiary does not lend, this is treated as a close proxy for Solo and is flagged in that year's quarterly file and below. Q1-Q3 UNAUDITED QUARTERLY INTERIM FILINGS (FY2016, FY2023-FY2025, sourced in a later pass) independently confirm the same basis choice: each interim filing's own 'Balance Sheet (Unaudited)'/'Profit and Loss Account (Unaudited)' pages (used throughout this dataset) are explicitly the plain, non-Consolidated statements, printed immediately after (and clearly distinguished from) a separate 'Consolidated Balance Sheet (Unaudited)'/'Consolidated Profit and Loss Account (Unaudited)' section earlier in the same PDF from FY2023 onward; FY2016 predates the subsidiary entirely and has no Consolidated section to distinguish from. Unlike the FY2025 ANNUAL report (whose classified-loans citation was Consolidated-only, see above), each 2025 quarter's classified-loans/NPL figures come from the interim filing's own Note 8.11 'Classification of loans', positioned within the Solo notes section of the document (well before that filing's separate, later Consolidated notes package) -- confirmed Solo-basis by an explicit 'on solo basis' capital-related sentence on or near the same note page in the quarters spot-checked for this phrase (2024_Q1.json, 2025_Q2.json), and by consistent document-structure position in the remainder.
sources.notes: South Bangla Agriculture and Commerce Bank Ltd. (renamed SBAC Bank PLC in 2023) was incorporated on 20 February 2013 and obtained its banking licence on 25 March 2013, so FY2013 is its first year of operation; there is no FY2011 or FY2012 for this bank and this 13-year series (FY2013-FY2025) is its entire public history. All 13 years were sourced from annual reports already present in annual_reports/SBACBANK/ (extracted by a prior session; this session performed no downloading, only extraction/structuring). Twelve of the thirteen years come from that year's own annual report; FY2017 is the exception (see below). A pervasive, well-diagnosed and non-erroneous data-quality pattern affects EPS and (less consistently) Net Asset Value per share across almost every year: this bank issues near-annual stock dividends (bonus shares) at rates disclosed in its own dividend-history table (6% in 2016, 15% in 2016-for-2017-issue, 13.50% in 2017-for-2018-issue, 10% in 2018-for-2019-issue, 10% in 2019-for-2020-issue, 4% in 2020-for-2021-issue, 1% in 2021-for-2022-issue), and under BAS 33 each bonus issue requires EPS for ALL prior comparative periods to be recalculated using the enlarged share count. This dataset independently reproduced the mechanism for four separate years (FY2015: 0.88 original vs 0.83 restated in the FY2016 report, reconciling to PAT/post-6%-bonus-shares exactly; FY2016: 2.19 original vs 1.90 restated in the FY2019 report; FY2017: 1.97 (derived, at FY2017 year-end share count) vs 1.74 restated in the FY2019 report; FY2018: 1.55 original vs 1.41 restated in the FY2019 report's own audited P&L comparative column) and found every restatement to be arithmetically exact once the correct post-bonus share count is applied. Separately, and NOT explained by the bonus mechanism, this bank's own Directors'-Report narrative 'Key Financial Indicators' 5-year tables are internally inconsistent with its own audited P&L comparative column in the SAME annual report on this point (e.g. the FY2019 report's audited P&L restates FY2018 EPS to 1.41, but that same report's own 5-year narrative table still shows FY2018 as 1.55, unrestated) and are inconsistent with EACH OTHER across report vintages for the same historical year (the FY2019 report's 5-year table shows FY2016=1.90 and FY2017=1.74; the FY2020 report's 5-year table instead shows FY2016=2.19 and FY2017=1.97 -- i.e. UNrestated -- for the identical years). This dataset resolves the ambiguity by using each fiscal year's own first-published (contemporaneous, pre-future-bonus) EPS as reported in that year's own annual report throughout, and documents every specific instance of divergence found in that year's quarterly JSON's period_note rather than silently reconciling. Net Asset Value per share shows the same pattern in at least two instances (FY2018: 13.13 original vs 11.94 restated in the FY2019 report; FY2019: 13.44 original vs 12.22 restated in the FY2020 report) but NOT in others (FY2015's NAV of 11.93 is unchanged in the FY2016 report despite the 6% bonus that same year) -- i.e. the bank's own restatement practice for NAV is itself inconsistent from year to year, unlike EPS where every checked instance was bonus-adjusted.

sources.period: Bank-wide finding: multi-year regulatory-forbearance letter pattern on the loans-and-advances provision shortfall
sources.note: Every quarterly filing's Note 8.10 (Required provision for loans, advances and lease/investments) footnote cites a Bangladesh Bank Department of Off-site Supervision letter (ref. DOS(CAMS)1157/41(dividend)/YYYY-NNNN) approving deferral of that year's provision shortfall until the next annual financial statements are finalized. Three consecutive years of these letters were found: 2023-2113 (25 Apr 2023, ~Tk.370m gap for FY2022/23), 2024-1836 (30 Apr 2024, ~Tk.355.6m gap for FY2023, later a much larger Tk.6,558.4m gap emerged within FY2024 itself, disclosed via a separate DBI-3/132/2024-640 letter and a subsequent 2025-3115 DOS letter), and 2025-3115 (22 May 2025, the resulting Tk.11,430.1m all-loans-and-advances gap allowing FY2024 to be finalized without full provisioning -- this is the same letter quoted in the FY2025 quarterly filings and reflected in 2025_Q4.json's auditor's qualified opinion). The FULL loans-and-advances-only shortfall trajectory reconstructed across all quarterly and annual filings in this dataset: -370.0m (Dec-2022) -> -370.0m (Mar-2023) -> -369.9m (Jun-2023) -> -277.4m (Sep-2023) -> -355.64m (Dec-2023, per 2024_Q1.json's comparative) -> -266.73m (Mar-2024) -> -182.68m (Jun-2024) -> -77.39m (Sep-2024) -> -6,558.39m (Dec-2024, an approximately 85x single-quarter explosion) -> -6,556.94m (Mar-2025, flat) -> -7,361.52m (Jun-2025) -> -8,019.93m (Sep-2025). This full multi-year, multi-quarter series is the single clearest, most granular evidence in this dataset of how a provisioning gap can be repeatedly deferred by regulatory letter while compounding underneath, and of exactly which reporting periods concealed vs. revealed the deterioration.

2013-2015 and 2016 Q1: confirmed UNAVAILABLE, not merely unresearched -- the bank's own investors-relations document list (see the 2016 Q2/Q3 entry above) shows no quarterly interim filings exist for these periods at all (only Annual Report + Auditors' Report). 2017 Q1-Q3, 2018 Q1-Q3, 2019 Q1-Q3, 2020 Q1-Q3, 2021 Q1-Q3, 2022 Q1-Q2 (2022 Q3 also confirmed unavailable/not listed on the bank's site) DO exist as listed, downloadable PDFs at the same https://cdn.sbacbank.com/files/investors-relations/financial-statement-YYYY-qN.pdf URL pattern (confirmed present in the site's own document listing) but were not reached in this pass -- prioritization went to FY2023-2025 per the task's explicit instruction, plus 2016 Q2/Q3 as a low-cost bonus already in hand from the same site-discovery step. 2026 Q1/Q2 also exist on the site (most recent filings, dated within this dataset's 'current date') but were similarly not reached. All of these remain a genuine, addressable gap for a future session -- not a case of non-existence like 2013-2015Q1/2016Q1.
